subject: turn decisions depend on the asynchronous semantic-promotion boundary

architectural_cause.mechanism: Deliberate two-phase design in src/baxy_mind/__main__.py: the sidecar starts with a lexical-only PlannerCatalog (encoder=None, line ~2542) and promote_planner_resources swaps in the semantic catalog only after TurnEvidenceService leaves 'building' and the E5 router reports ready (line ~2401). Until then candidate_families() returns () and retrieve() returns [], and PlannerCatalog._semantic_scores silently returns {} on encoder failure - all advisory fallbacks that nevertheless change the P prompt composition.
architectural_cause.boundary_timing: turn.evidence.status reports building->ready at 19.33s and 21.82s after catalog.configure in two fresh sessions; the vector disk cache (LOCALAPPDATA/BAXYRuntime/turn-evidence, 38.6 MB, hit) means the E5 worker spin-up dominates the window, which is an asset/hardware floor, not an internal knob.
architectural_cause.consequence: every session serves its first ~20s of turns in the degraded lexical regime; in the frozen 30-turn workload turns 00-03 always run lexical, turn-04 straddles the boundary (explains its bimodal 15/30 retry rate), and later turns run semantic

instability_evidence.same_text_two_decisions: turn-23 alone: cold index -> conversation, 1 attempt, 4.77s (prompt sha 10700527); settled index -> clarify, 2 attempts, 19.51s with deterministic thinking drain (prompt sha e18ff2be)

variants.variant: V-A: gate turn intake on semantic readiness (turns wait until status=ready plus promotion margin)
variants.corpus_run: evidence_ready_gated_workload_20260730.json - full frozen 30-turn workload, 30/30 valid, 0 validation errors, p50 5.587s / p95 19.502s / max 19.523s
variants.time_dependence: eliminated by construction: every turn executes in the certified semantic regime regardless of arrival time
decision_diffs_vs_recorded_baseline: turn-06 (cuanta vram se esta usando): clarify(2 attempts) -> conversation(1)
variants.reading: the two diffs are exactly early/boundary turns whose recorded baseline decisions came from the lexical regime; whether the semantic-regime decisions are corrections requires oracle (final39-class) adjudication. turn-06 also shows that within the semantic regime cache-state nondeterminism still flips the drain (consistent with its 27/30 historical rate), so V-A stabilizes the regime, not the model's numeric sensitivity
variants.cost: first turn availability delayed up to ~19-22s after catalog; a product/SLA decision, not an internal optimization
promotion_blockers: oracle adjudication of the early-turn decision flips
startup-availability SLA change requires explicit product authorization
full exhaustive corpus run (final39-class) - the 30-turn frozen workload is necessary but not sufficient for promotion

variants.reason: reverts the certified evidence quality wins (final scheduler preflight showed evidence gains a critical case); changes far more decisions than V-A

variants.variant: V-C: make readiness faster until blocking is cheap
variants.reason: the vector cache already hits; the window is dominated by E5 worker spin-up (model load), which cannot be reduced without changing the encoder asset/runtime - outside internal scope

variants.variant: V-D: bounded partial waits inside candidate_families/retrieve
variants.reason: narrows but does not eliminate the time dependence, failing the stability criterion

verdict: Cause proven and characterized; V-A is the only variant that eliminates the time dependence and it works physically (30/30 valid, all turns in the certified regime), but it is not promotable without oracle adjudication of the early-turn decision changes and an explicit product decision on delayed first-turn availability. Registered as an open product-behavior decision, not silently patched.
